The samples were then exposed to light (1500 lumens) and/or heat (85°C), and light transmittance was measured over time using a spectrophotometer. Higher transmittance is correlated to lighter color. Only the “Light only” group shows an obvious and continuous rise, indicating that chloroplasts only when there is light and no heat treatment have photosynthesis obviously promoted; heating alone or heating plus light did not produce a similar effect.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a results table of transmittance (%) over time for four chloroplast/DPIP treatments. Compare each treatment’s initial and final transmittance. Note that only the light-only treatment shows a strong, sustained increase, from about 20.8% at 0 min to 77.5% at 20 min, while the no-light/no-heat, heat-only, and light-plus-heat treatments remain nearly flat in the low 20s. Use the prompt’s statement that higher transmittance means lighter color, plus the DPIP indicator rule, to infer that photosynthetic electron transport occurred mainly in the light-only tube. Conclude that photosynthesis is stimulated when chloroplasts are exposed to light only.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中是一张“Transmittance (%)”结果表，按时间0、5、10、15、20 min列出4种处理：No light and no heat、Light only、Heat only、Both light and heat。表中可读到，Light only组的透光率从20.8%持续升到37.8%、48.7%、63.4%、77.5%；而No light and no heat组大致在23.2%到25.7%之间波动，Heat only组大致在20.4%到22.1%之间波动，Both light and heat组大致在20.4%到23.0%之间波动。
再推理：题干说明透光率越高颜色越浅。DPIP在光合作用电子传递中会被还原，颜色变浅、透光率升高，因此透光率持续上升表示光合作用电子传递更活跃。只有“Light only”组出现明显且持续的上升，说明 chloroplasts 只有在有光而无热处理时，光合作用被明显促进；单独加热或加热加光都没有产生类似效果。

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a four-column treatment table with transmittance measured at 0–20 minutes. Treat the columns as a factorial experiment: no light/no heat is the baseline, light only tests light without heat, heat only tests heat without light, and both light and heat tests whether heat plus light has the same effect. Compare light only to the baseline and observe a large rise to 77.5%, showing light can stimulate the process. Compare heat only to the baseline and observe only small low-20% values, so heat alone does not stimulate it. Compare both light and heat to light only and observe the heated light sample remains near 23%, so heat does not enhance photosynthesis and likely inhibits the light response. Therefore the reasonable conclusion is that photosynthesis is stimulated only in chloroplasts exposed to light without heat.
